investigationEvent.text: TC-M08: Patient B.P. (female neonate, born 2026-03-05, 79 days at report) born at 34 weeks gestation to mother Sarah P. (28y, rheumatoid arthritis). Mother received Testdrugimab 200mg SC biweekly (combination product with Testdevice Auto-Injector) starting at gestation week 20 (2025-10-01) for RA; drug withdrawn at delivery. Auto-injector malfunctioned on first use. Neonate admitted to NICU: thrombocytopenia (platelets 45e9/L day 1) and low birth weight (1.95 kg). Platelets recovered by day 14. Sender diagnosis: Neonatal thrombocytopenia secondary to in utero Testdrugimab exposure. D.10 parent data, G.k.6a/b gestation, F.r LOINC codes, device model/serial included.

observationEvent.value: Neonatal thrombocytopenia and low birth weight are consistent with in utero immunosuppressant exposure to Testdrugimab during the 2nd and 3rd trimesters. The auto-injector device malfunction on first use may have caused inconsistent drug delivery. The causal relationship is plausible given the known immunosuppressive mechanism of action. Platelet count normalized by day 14 post-delivery without pharmacological intervention.

(28y, RA) received Testdrugimab 200mg SC biweekly from gestation week 20 to delivery; auto-injector device malfunction on first use. Neonate B.P. (female, 34 wks, 1.95 kg) born with thrombocytopenia (platelets 45e9/L) requiring NICU. Platelet count normalized by day 14. Cumulative maternal dose: 21800mg.

Mother Sarah P. (28y) was treated with Testdrugimab 200mg SC biweekly from gestation week 20 for rheumatoid arthritis. Methotrexate had been discontinued prior to conception. The auto-injector device malfunctioned on first use. Neonate B.P. was delivered prematurely at 34 weeks, birth weight 1.95 kg. Neonatal thrombocytopenia (platelets 45e9/L) and low birth weight were observed. NICU admission required. Platelet count normalized by day 14 without specific treatment. Reporter concludes Testdrugimab is the likely cause of neonatal thrombocytopenia through transplacental immunosuppression.
